That also means I can miss questions, so if I do, try rephrasing or use the Email me button.

entries.title: Who is Nitin
entries.k: who is nitin jha about introduce yourself tell me about him bio background summary overview what does he do
entries.ex: who is nitin; tell me about nitin; what does nitin do; is nitin a phd student
entries.a: Nitin Jha is a PhD student in Computer Science at Kennesaw State University in Georgia, working under Dr. Abhishek Parakh. He researches quantum networks and quantum key distribution, and how to make quantum-secured communication practical on real networks. He has a physics background from Ashoka University.

entries.title: Research
entries.k: research work focus interests topics area study studying working on themes field protocol protocols design designs
entries.ex: what does nitin research; what is his research about; what is he working on
entries.a: Nitin works on quantum networks and quantum key distribution. His main thread is quantum-augmented networks: today's classical networks with quantum protocols added where they matter, since fully quantum networks aren't practical yet. That covers protocol design, the effect of noise and topology, quantum error correction, and quantum-secured defenses for things like microgrids.

entries.title: What is QKD
entries.k: qkd quantum key distribution what is explain key distribution bb84 secret key eavesdropping eve
entries.a: Quantum key distribution lets two parties agree on a shared secret key using quantum states. Because measuring a quantum state disturbs it, an eavesdropper leaves detectable traces. Nitin's QKD review in Cryptologia covers the main protocol families and their known attacks.

entries.title: Three-stage protocol
entries.k: three-stage three stage protocol kak kaks lock commutative encryption box no key exchange
entries.a: Kak's three-stage protocol sends a message securely without ever sharing a key. Alice locks it with her own operation and sends it to Bob, Bob adds his lock and sends it back, Alice removes hers, and Bob finally removes his. It works because the two locks commute. It also tolerates multi-photon pulses, which is why Nitin studies it for practical networks.

entries.title: Quantum-augmented network
entries.k: quantum-augmented augmented quanet quanets network hybrid quantum-classical what is add
entries.a: A quantum-augmented network (QuANet) is a classical network with quantum protocols added where they matter most, like key distribution or secure direct communication for the most sensitive traffic. It's a practical near-term route because a fully quantum network needs hardware that doesn't exist at scale yet. It's the running theme of Nitin's research.

entries.title: CSS error correction
entries.k: css calderbank shor steane error correction quantum errors bit flip phase flip syndrome fix codes qecc
entries.a: CSS (Calderbank-Shor-Steane) codes are quantum error-correcting codes that fix bit-flip and phase-flip errors by measuring error syndromes, without ever measuring the data itself. Nitin combines them with the three-stage protocol so encryption and error correction happen in one step.

entries.title: Quantum anonymous notification
entries.k: anonymous notification qan ghz state states entangled notify receiver anonymity sender who is sending
entries.a: Quantum anonymous notification lets a sender tell a receiver that a quantum message is coming without revealing who is talking to whom. Nitin's improved version uses rotations on shared GHZ states (a kind of multi-party entangled state) and holds up better against dephasing noise.

entries.title: Steganography
entries.k: steganography steganalysis stego hidden hiding cover payload detect audio video
entries.a: Steganography hides a secret message inside ordinary media like an image or video, and steganalysis tries to detect it. Nitin has looked at both a quantum hiding scheme (the Quantum Hilbert Transform) and how well detectors catch payloads split across audio and video.

entries.title: Microgrids
entries.k: microgrid microgrids smr small modular reactor islanded island grid-connected grid controller energy power
entries.a: A microgrid is a small local power system with its own generation, storage, and loads that can run connected to the main grid or on its own. In Nitin's work they're powered by small modular reactors, plus solar and wind, and run by controllers that talk over classical and quantum links.

entries.title: Islanded mode
entries.k: islanded islanding island mode disconnected grid-connected connected import utility
entries.a: Islanded mode means a microgrid is cut off from the utility grid and runs only on its own generation and storage. In grid-connected mode it can import a limited amount of power (35 kW per microgrid in his simulator). In a simulated 10-minute islanding event, battery charge dropped from 15 to 5 kWh and peak unserved load rose from 25 to 60 kW.

entries.title: Post-quantum cryptography
entries.k: post-quantum post quantum cryptography pqc crypto tls pki lattice classical algorithms resist
entries.a: Post-quantum cryptography means classical algorithms designed to stay secure even against quantum computers. Nitin covers it, along with TLS and blockchain security, in his video series.

entries.title: Multi-photon protocols
entries.k: multi-photon multiphoton photon photons single-photon emitter burst decoy e91
entries.a: Multi-photon protocols like the three-stage protocol don't need ideal single-photon sources, which makes them easier to deploy over existing infrastructure. Nitin studies how far and how fast they work under noise and across different network topologies.

entries.title: Microgrid demo
entries.k: microgrid demo animation interactive zoom islanded grid-connected
entries.a: The microgrid demo is a 9-step tour of a network of SMR-powered microgrids. It zooms into one microgrid's generation, storage, loads, and controller, zooms back out to the quantum and classical links between controllers, then shows grid-connected and islanded modes and how the quantum defense blocks a spoofed command.

entries.title: Microgrid paper
entries.k: microgrid cybersecurity framework quam spie 2026 paudel small modular reactor smr attack spoofing false data injection qca ping-pong defense paper
entries.a: 'A Novel Quantum Augmented Framework to Improve Microgrid Cybersecurity' (SPIE 2026, with Prateek Paudel, Dr. Parakh, and Mahadevan Subramaniam) builds QuAM, a simulator for microgrids powered by small modular reactors. It layers physical power, communication, quantum security, and attacks, then tests spoofing and false-data attacks in grid-connected and islanded modes. The full quantum defense blocked all simulated spoofed commands and cut energy-not-served from about 52 kWh to about 12 kWh, for roughly 35 ms of extra latency. Quantum-authenticated control tokens mattered most.
entries.chip: Tell me about the microgrid paper

entries.title: GAN paper
entries.k: gan gans generative adversarial hybrid quantum-classical network flows traffic intrusion detection unsw variational generator adversarial network paudel paper
entries.a: 'Hybrid Quantum-Classical GANs for the Generation of Adversarial Network Flows' (SPIE 2026, with Prateek Paudel) uses a variational quantum generator to create synthetic malicious traffic from latent vectors encoded as quantum states. A classical discriminator trains against it on UNSW-NB15 data, to study how well such traffic evades intrusion detection and how hardware noise affects the attack.
entries.chip: What is the GAN paper about?

entries.title: Steganalysis paper
entries.k: steganalysis steganography multimodal split-payload audiovisual audio video detectors evade imns paudel paper
entries.a: 'Evaluating Multimodal Steganalysis for Split-Payload Audiovisual Steganography' (with Prateek Paudel, accepted to IEEE IMNS) asks whether splitting a secret between audio and video helps it evade detectors. Single-mode detectors were near random guessing, and multimodal detectors improved mostly by using the video stream rather than a real joint audio-video signal.
entries.chip: Tell me about the steganalysis paper

entries.title: Quantum voting paper
entries.k: voting vote election elections ballot ballots tally quantum voting protocols practical ubiquity paper
entries.a: 'Are Quantum Voting Protocols Practical?' (with Dr. Parakh) surveys quantum voting schemes that promise ballot secrecy and verifiable tallies from quantum physics rather than computational hardness. It reviews the main families and the obstacles (loss, noise, imperfect devices, scaling) and concludes with realistic scenarios for small elections. It's an arXiv preprint.

entries.title: Quantum Hilbert Transform
entries.k: hilbert transform quantum hilbert qht signal processing phase shift steganography scheme paper
entries.a: 'Quantum Hilbert Transform' (with Dr. Parakh) introduces a quantum version of the classical Hilbert transform, a signal-processing operation that had no quantum counterpart, and demonstrates it on a quantum steganography task. It points toward quantum signal processing, sensing, and secure information hiding.
entries.chip: Tell me about the Hilbert transform paper

entries.title: Aerial quantum networks
entries.k: aerial drones drone balloons satellites satellite global quantum internet ieee potentials free-space review air paper
entries.a: 'Towards a Global Quantum Internet: A Review of Challenges Facing Aerial Quantum Networks' (IEEE Potentials, 2025, with Dr. Parakh) looks at using drones, high-altitude balloons, and satellites to extend quantum networks beyond fixed ground links. It covers the engineering challenges and proposes combining ground stations, aerial relays, and satellites into one architecture.

entries.title: QKD review
entries.k: qkd review cryptologia security proofs practical attacks bb84 continuous-variable twin-field device-independent survey paper
entries.a: 'Quantum Key Distribution: Bridging Theoretical Security Proofs, Practical Attacks, and Error Correction for Quantum-Augmented Networks' (Cryptologia, 2026) is a long review of QKD families: BB84-style, three-stage, continuous-variable, twin-field, and device-independent. It emphasizes security proofs and known attacks, and connects them to quantum error correction and quantum-augmented networks.
entries.chip: Tell me about the QKD review

entries.title: Anonymous notification paper
entries.k: anonymous notification protocol improved frontiers ghz state rotation dephasing false notifications qan quantum-augmented paper
entries.a: 'An Improved Quantum Anonymous Notification Protocol for Quantum-Augmented Networks' (Frontiers in Quantum Science and Technology, 2026) uses rotation operations on shared GHZ states to anonymously notify receivers in an n-user network. It resists false notifications better under dephasing noise, and it's designed to work with an ML classifier in a QuANet so headers leak less information.

entries.title: Joint encryption paper
entries.k: joint encryption error correction jeec scientific reports css three-stage nature 2024 integrated paper
entries.a: 'Joint Encryption and Error Correction for Secure Quantum Communication' (Scientific Reports, 2024) extends the three-stage protocol with CSS error-correcting codes so encryption and error correction are one process instead of two. It fixes single bit-flip and phase-flip errors and works for arbitrary qubits.
entries.chip: Tell me about the joint encryption paper

entries.title: Noise and topologies paper
entries.k: noise topologies topology ring star torus repeater placement spie photonics west 2024 channel device paper
entries.a: 'Effect of Noise and Topologies on Multi-Photon Quantum Protocols' (SPIE Photonics West 2024) studies how channel and device noise affect the three-stage protocol in ring, star, and torus networks, in terms of security, distance, and bit rate. It gives practical guidance on repeater placement and topology choice.
entries.chip: Tell me about the noise and topologies paper

entries.title: ML HTTP paper
entries.k: http protocol machine learning ml nlp qce ieee poster packet payload classify sensitive 2024 quantum augmented http paper
entries.a: 'A ML Based Approach to Quantum Augmented HTTP Protocol' (IEEE QCE 2024 poster) proposes changing the HTTP packet structure to carry both classical and quantum payloads. An NLP model rates how sensitive each message is, and only sensitive content goes through the quantum channel. There's no arXiv version, but his SPIE 2025 paper builds on the same idea.

entries.title: Quantum-classical augmented network paper
entries.k: augmented network towards quantum-classical http classical quantum payload privacy label logistic regression cnn lstm bilstm spie photonics west 2025 paper
entries.a: 'Towards a Quantum-Classical Augmented Network' (SPIE Photonics West 2025) expands the HTTP idea: one packet carries classical and quantum payloads split by privacy need. Models like logistic regression, CNN, LSTM, and BiLSTM classify each message's privacy label, so quantum resources are used only where they're needed.
entries.chip: Tell me about the augmented network paper

entries.title: Multi-photon QKD paper
entries.k: multi-photon qkd practical infocommunications journal decoy-state e91 topologies burst distance emitters 2025 paper
entries.a: 'Multi-Photon QKD for Practical Quantum Networks' (Infocommunications Journal, 2025) evaluates the three-stage, decoy-state, and E91 protocols across direct, line, grid, ring, and torus topologies under multi-photon bursts. It relates burst size to the maximum stable distance, which removes the need for single-photon emitters.
